Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, Nxeon hosting platform). FIRST STEP: create your own isolated git worktree so you don't collide with parallel work happening on this same repo right now:
  cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-invedit -b feature/freemc-inventory main
Then `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-invedit`, symlink node_modules from the primary tree if it's not already usable (`ls node_modules` — if missing/broken: `ln -s /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules`), and symlink the env: `ln -s /opt/nxeon/.env .env` if `.env` isn't present. Do ALL your work in this worktree, not in /opt/nxeon directly.

This worktree already has a 12-mode "free Minecraft server" product on main (commit c2e97e9): one free Docker-based Minecraft server per account, on a dedicated VM ("freemc-host", a real `Server` row with `hostname="freemc-host"`), running itzg/mc-router in front of itzg/minecraft-server containers, managed via RCON.

READ FIRST, in full: `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` and `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`. Key patterns you must follow:
- `sendRcon(host, containerName, userId, command)` in free-minecraft-control.ts is the existing helper that runs `docker exec <container> rcon-cli <cmd>` over SSH — reuse it exactly, don't reinvent RCON plumbing.
- `getFreeServerPlayers` — existing helper returning currently-online players via `rcon-cli list`.
- `rconPasswordFor(userId)` — deterministic RCON password (scrypt-derived, never stored).
- `shellQuote` (from `lib/ssh-exec.ts`) wraps every value interpolated into a remote shell command — never build an RCON/shell command from unescaped or unvalidated input. This matters even more for RCON: you're constructing a Minecraft command string, and while `rcon-cli` itself isn't a shell, sloppy string-building could still let a crafted item id or slot name produce a malformed/unexpected command, so validate everything against fixed allowlists before use.
- `withServerSsh(host, async (conn) => {...})` + `exec(conn, cmd, timeoutMs)` — how SSH commands run. Get the host via `db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" } })`.
- `FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION = "26.1.2"` — pin this VERSION on any plugins-kind test container you boot.

YOUR TASK — build a player inventory editor for the Players tab.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT to research and confirm, then design around: vanilla Minecraft RCON has no native "read a player's current inventory" command. The only inventory-WRITE primitive is (from 1.19+) `/item replace entity <player> <slot> with <item>[<count>]`, where `<slot>` is one of `weapon.mainhand`, `weapon.offhand`, `armor.head`, `armor.chest`, `armor.legs`, `armor.feet`, `inventory.0` through `inventory.35`, or `hotbar.0` through `hotbar.8`. Confirm this syntax is correct (check current Minecraft command docs/changelog for the `/item` command — it's been stable since 1.19 but verify slot names precisely) and that `with air` clears a slot (equivalent to deleting an item). Given there's no read-back, design the editor as an explicit "set this slot to become X" tool, NOT a live view+edit of current contents — be upfront about that limitation in the UI copy rather than implying it shows current inventory state.

1. Build `lib/minecraft-items.ts` — a reasonably complete curated `MINECRAFT_ITEMS: { id: string; label: string; category: string }[]` covering common tools/weapons/armor/blocks/food/valuables/redstone (a few hundred entries is fine, doesn't need to be all ~1400 vanilla items — prioritize what a player would actually want to grant: diamond/netherite gear, enchanted-adjacent base items, common blocks, food, valuables like diamonds/emeralds/netherite ingots, potions, etc). Every `id` must be a real `minecraft:`-namespaced item id.

2. Build `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts` — `"use server"`:
   - `applyPlayerInventoryEdit(prev, formData)`: `requireUser()`, load caller's `FreeMinecraftServer`, validate the target player name is currently online (via `getFreeServerPlayers` — refuse if not, with a clear error), validate the slot name against a fixed allowlist (the exact slot list above — reject anything else), validate the item id against `MINECRAFT_ITEMS` (reject anything not in the catalog), validate count is an integer 1-64, then call `sendRcon` with the constructed `/item replace entity <player> <slot> with <item> <count>` (or `with air` if clearing). Rate-limit reasonably (reuse `checkRateLimit` from `lib/rate-limit.ts` the way other actions in `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` do) since this fires real commands against a live server.
   - Consider whether to support a batch/multi-slot submission (apply several slot changes in one action call) vs one-at-a-time — either is fine, pick what's cleanest for the UI you build.

3. Build `components/customer/freemc/InventoryEditor.tsx` — `"use client"`. Player picker (from the currently-online players list — reuse the same online-players fetch pattern as the existing `Players` component in `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx`, read that file for the exact style/pattern), then a slot grid (armor + offhand + 36 main inventory, laid out sensibly) where each slot has an item search/select (from `MINECRAFT_ITEMS`, needs to be searchable/filterable given the catalog size — a simple filtered dropdown or combobox is fine) and a count field, plus an explicit UI note that this SETS slots rather than showing current contents. Match the existing Tailwind visual style in `FreeMcDashboard.tsx` (`card`, `btn-primary`, `input` utility classes, dark navy theme).

4. Live-test what you actually CAN verify headlessly (no real Minecraft client available to you): boot a real test container on freemc-host (container name `mc-invtest`, any preset, VERSION=26.1.2 if plugins-kind, ENABLE_RCON=true), confirm via `sendRcon`-equivalent (or plain `docker exec ... rcon-cli`) that `/item replace entity <nonexistent-player> inventory.0 with minecraft:diamond 1` returns Minecraft's normal graceful "no entity found" response rather than crashing the server or erroring the RCON connection — this at least proves the command syntax is accepted server-side. Be explicit in your final report that full end-to-end behavior (a real online player actually receiving the item) is "syntax-verified, not player-verified" since you have no way to connect an actual Minecraft client. Clean up your test container/data dir and any throwaway scripts before finishing.

5. Do NOT edit `FreeMcDashboard.tsx`, `actions-free-minecraft.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, or any other existing file — only create the new files above. Do NOT merge to main or push anywhere. Do NOT delete your worktree when done — I'll integrate from it and clean it up myself.

6. Before finishing: `npx tsc --noEmit` and a full `npm run build` in your worktree must both pass clean. Commit your work in the worktree (git add the new files explicitly, never `git add -A`) so it's not lost.

Report back: the exact RCON command syntax you settled on and how you verified it, the file paths created, size/scope of the item catalog, the worktree path/branch name, and an honest note on what is and isn't truly end-to-end verified.

13	import type { Client } from "ssh2";
14	import { exec, execInput, shellQuote } from "./ssh-exec";

16	/**
17	 * Deterministic per-server RCON password — HMAC-shaped via scrypt off
18	 * AUTH_SECRET, same derivation pattern as lib/crypto-box.ts's BYOK key (just a
19	 * different domain-separation salt). Never stored: computed identically at
20	 * container-creation time and every time we need to talk RCON to it, so a
21	 * restart/recreate never invalidates it and there's nothing to leak from the DB.
22	 */
23	export function rconPasswordFor(ownerId: string): string {
24	  const secret = process.env.AUTH_SECRET;
25	  if (!secret || !secret.trim()) throw new Error("AUTH_SECRET is not set — cannot derive RCON password");
26	  return scryptSync(secret, `nxeon-freemc-rcon:${ownerId}`, 24).toString("base64url");
27	}

29	/** Run one command inside a container via `docker exec`. */
30	async function dockerExec(conn: Client, containerName: string, cmd: string, timeoutMs = 15_000) {
31	  return exec(conn, `docker exec ${shellQuote(containerName)} ${cmd}`, timeoutMs);
32	}

37	};

41	 * ping, no RCON auth needed. A stopped/sleeping container (mc-router scaled it
42	 * to zero) just fails the docker exec, which reads as "not running", not an
43	 * error — that's the expected, common state for a free server nobody's on.
44	 */
45	export async function getFreeServerStatus(conn: Client, containerName: string): Promise<ServerStatus> {
46	  const inspect = await exec(
47	    conn,
48	    `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`,
49	    10_000,
50	  );
51	  if (inspect.code !== 0 || inspect.stdout.trim() !== "true") {

58	    10_000,

66	    }
